title: edge-fallback-lease-and-degraded-mode-contract
author: Aisha Patel
content:
## Summary

This document defines the "Edge Fallback Lease" and the "Degraded Mode Contract" for Redwood's inference mesh. The goal is to provide a clear, implementable contract across API clients, edge proxies, regional routers, and runtime shards so that when primary model variants or capacity are unavailable we can: (1) degrade gracefully with bounded latency/quality trade-offs, (2) maintain transparent cost attribution, and (3) avoid systemic cascades.

This is an architecture + infra standard with specific API semantics, runtime configuration, observability requirements, and rollout/rollback procedures. It is intended for edge, API gateway, routing, and serving runtime owners.

## Context and motivation
- Increasing multi-variant serving and cross-region fallback paths introduced complexity when a single upstream failure caused noisy, indefinite fallbacks.
- Clients need predictable semantics: when a fallback occurs, they should receive a deterministic response shape, a clear TTL indicating how long the fallback decision is valid, and telemetry to explain the quality/latency impact.
- Operators need bounded resource impact: fallback decisions must prevent request amplification and ensure caches/leases expire in a controlled window.

## Goals
- Provide a small, composable contract that can be applied at edge, proxy, and shard levels.
- Keep client-visible surface minimal: a fallback indicator, a lease TTL, and optional suggested model/hint.
- Ensure fallbacks are reversible and observable (metrics, traces, logs).
- Minimize cost by preferring cheaper quantized variants when appropriate, but only under explicit policy.

## Non-goals
- This standard does not replace model quality evals or business-level routing policies (those live in Optimize/playbooks).
- It does not mandate an exact algorithm for fallback scoring — only the signals that must be produced and consumed.

## Contract: Edge Fallback Lease (EFL)

A short, machine-readable lease object is attached to responses when an upstream routing decision has chosen a fallback path (model variant, region, or degraded inference mode). The lease guarantees the fallback decision is valid for a bounded time window and provides provenance and quality hints.

Semantic guarantees:
- TTL semantics: lease_ttl_ms is the authoritative maximum duration the client/edge may assume the fallback decision remains valid. After expiry clients MUST treat results as potentially stale and re-evaluate routing.
- Idempotency: leases include a stable lease_id generated by the decision plane. Replaying a request with the same lease_id should not produce additional accounting spikes in routing logs.
- Non-amplification: a lease flags whether it is cacheable at proxies (cacheable: true|false). Cacheable leases may be reused only within the same tenant and route.

API surface (response-level fields)
- fallback_reason: string (human-readable short code, e.g., "variant_unavailable", "region_overload", "preemption_detected", "quality_threshold_exceeded")
- lease_id: string (opaque decision-plane UUID v4)
- lease_ttl_ms: integer (milliseconds)
- fallback_model: string (optional; canonical model id used for fallback)
- cacheable: boolean

Example response snippet (JSON):
{
  "response": "...",
  "fallback_reason": "variant_unavailable",
  "lease_id": "3f9a2b4e-1a4e-4c6b-8b90-2b9d3b9e5a2f",
  "lease_ttl_ms": 3000,
  "fallback_model": "redwood:gptx-quant-8bit-v2",
  "cacheable": false
}

## Degraded Mode Contract (DMC)

Degraded Mode refers to a controlled runtime configuration where quality is intentionally decreased to preserve latency/SLOs and reduce cost. DMC defines the expected behavior for routes flagged as eligible for degradation.

Policy knobs (per-route):
- degrade_allowed: boolean (enabled per customer/route)
- degrade_max_quality_drop_pct: integer (0-100; measured against eval baseline)
- degrade_priority: integer (1..100; higher means more likely to be degraded under pressure)
- degrade_fallback_models: ordered list of model ids

Behavioral guarantees:
- If degrade_allowed is false, runtime must return an error or apply alternate routing (no silent quality reductions).
- When degradation is applied, a DMC header must be emitted: dmc_applied=true and dmc_profile="<profile-id>".
- DMC must never be applied in stealth mode: the client must be able to detect degradation via the header and related metrics.

## Runtime & Infra configuration table
| name | description | recommended default | unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fallback_lease_ttl_ms | maximum EFL TTL generated at edge | 3000 | ms |
| fallback_idempotency_window_ms | window to dedupe billing/attribution for lease_id | 5000 | ms |
| degrade_max_route_share_pct | fraction of traffic that may be degraded for a route during steady-state | 20 | percent |
| degrade_eviction_backoff_ms | how quickly to revert degraded sessions on improved capacity | 10000 | ms |
| lease_cacheable_by_default | default cacheability for generated leases | false | boolean |

## Observability and SLOs

Required metrics (to be emitted by edge/proxy and runtime):
- ef_lease_emitted_count{route,tenant,fallback_reason}
- ef_lease_reused_count{route,tenant}
- dmc_applied_count{route,tenant,profile}
- dmc_quality_regression_pct{route,tenant} (computed from eval hooks and golden prompt sets)
- dmc_latency_p95_ms{route,tenant}

SLIs/SLOs for fallback behavior (examples):
- Correct fallback signalling: 99.9% of fallback responses must contain lease_id and lease_ttl_ms when fallback is used (SLO: 99.9/30d).
- Lease expiry accuracy: 99.5% of leases must not be used after lease_ttl_ms + 200ms.
- Degradation quality guardrail: average dmc_quality_regression_pct must be <= degrade_max_quality_drop_pct per route (SLO).

Tracing and logs:
- All fallback decisions must emit a decision trace span named "fallback.decision" with attributes: decision_plane_id, lease_id, fallback_reason, chosen_model, candidate_models, cost_estimate.
- Propagate lease_id as a trace tag across the request chain.

Alerting
- Alert on ef_lease_emitted_count spikes (>4x baseline) with runbook to inspect recent capacity events and circuit breakers.
- Alert when dmc_quality_regression_pct > configured threshold for more than 15 minutes.

## Operational runbook (summary)
1. Detection: Console alert or SLO breach triggers pager.
2. Triage: Check ef_lease_emitted_count and dmc_applied_count by region and shard.
3. Short-term mitigation: increase degrade_eviction_backoff_ms to avoid flip-flopping; prioritize canary rollback of new runtime kernel that increased preemptions.
4. Reversal: decide if route-level degrade_allowed should be toggled off for affected tenants (product decision).
5. Post-incident: run the regression triage playbook and attach findings to the incident ticket.

## Ownership and responsibilities
- Edge/Proxy team: implement EFL emission, trace propagation, and cacheability semantics.
- Routing/Decision Plane: generate lease_id and ensure idempotency dedupe.
- Serving runtime: honor cacheable flag and include dmc headers when degrading.
- Observability: own dashboards & alert rules for ef_lease_* and dmc_* metrics.
- Product: approve per-tenant degrade_allowed and degrade_max_quality_drop_pct settings.

## Testing checklist (preflight)
- Unit tests for lease generation, TTL boundaries, and cacheability flags.
- Integration test: simulate upstream variant failure and assert client sees fallback fields and decision trace.
- Load test: ensure ef_lease_emitted_count scales without causing billing amplification; validate idempotency window dedupe.
- Quality eval: run degraded profile against golden prompt set and assert regression <= configured threshold.

## Rollout and backward compatibility
- Phase 1 (canary): emit EFL headers only to 10% of traffic with a debug flag; do not change billing.
- Phase 2 (observe): enable idempotency dedupe in the accounting pipeline and validate no lost-attribution.
- Phase 3 (enforce): enable full cacheability semantics and reject incompatible clients (clients not acknowledging EFL when degrade_allowed=false receive 409).

Compatibility notes:
- Older clients that ignore fallback fields should continue to function; however they will not get the idempotency/billing dedupe benefits.
- Do not rely on lease_ttl_ms for long-lived sessions — leases are intentionally short.

## Failure modes and mitigations
- Stale leases used after expiry: ensure all proxies validate TTL on local clock and sync time via NTP; monitor lease expiry misses.
- Excessive reuse causing billing undercount: audit accounting logs against raw request traces and increase fallback_idempotency_window_ms cautiously.
- Silent degradation not signaled: create an automated smoke test that calls a set of golden prompts and verifies dmc_applied header presence when expected.

## Related decisions and references
- See runtime-flag contract and hot-reload guidance (related_pages above).
- This doc complements multi-variant contract and adaptive-quantization fallback standards.

## Appendix: sample CLI to inspect leases
Command to search traces with lease_id using internal trace tool:
internal-trace query --lease-id 3f9a2b4e-1a4e-4c6b-8b90-2b9d3b9e5a2f --time-window 15m

CLI to toggle route-level degrade_allowed (admin only):
redwood-admin route set --route-id <route> --degrade-allowed false --auth-token $ADMIN_TOKEN

End of document.
